memory_update.text: Keep PWR as the reference benchmark for grid EPC/services, but avoid letting it crowd out smaller contractor and component candidates.
MYRG and PRIM are the most relevant underfollowed contractor names for the epc_grid_services node because both have direct utility/power-delivery exposure and are smaller than Quanta.

PLPC should be tracked as a second-order upstream hardware candidate; survival in later layers requires verifying T&D revenue share, utility customer exposure, and correlation with contractor backlog.

Need a follow-up pass on private or partially hidden competitors such as MacLean Power Systems and other utility hardware suppliers to understand whether PLPC has genuine scarcity value as a public-market proxy.
Contractor backlog can be used as a leading demand signal for upstream grid hardware, but the timing relationship must be validated by product lead times, procurement cycles, and project delay risk.

node: EPC, construction, and grid services contractors
summary: Expanded the EPC/grid-services node using a two-lane funnel. Quanta remains the reference benchmark for craft-labor, transmission, renewables, and large-load execution capacity. The underfollowed lane is more interesting in smaller public contractors with utility/power-delivery backlogs, plus one second-order hardware supplier whose order intake may precede field construction. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
